body.statement: Using the handle \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{AC}}\), characterize every atom of \(S(h,Z_V)\) generated by flat hard-max strata and determine whether there exists a computable \(A(x)\downarrow0\) such that, uniformly over \(h\in\mathcal H\), \(V\in\mathcal K_V\), and \(q\in\mathbb R\), the probability of \(q<S(h,Z_V)\le q+x\) after removing the enumerated atom at \(q\) is at most \(A(x)\). If so, use it to make the algorithm return a two-sided least-favorable quantile bracket of prescribed value width.
body.justification: This is the genuinely open probability-theoretic step separating an honest conservative certificate from sharp quantile computation.
body.gap: CCK and Giessing prove concentration bounds for suprema of Gaussian coordinates or processes, not for the supremum of the nonlinear compactified Bregman path with flat hard cells.
body.consumer: A sharp modulus would bound excess conservativeness and certify the numerical distance to the ideal least-favorable critical value.
